name: Muhriz ibn al-Muka'bir
bio: Muhriz ibn al-Muka'bir, of Dabbah, celebrates in his ode the victory of his tribe with divisions of Tamim over Madhhij in the second battle of al-Kulab, probably fought in A.D. 611 or 612. He was not present at the battle.
Lyall adds that the poet was then a pagan but may have become a Muslim later in life.

poems.title: Ode LX: May all that I have amassed
poems.author: Muhriz ibn al-Muka'bir
poems.note: Lyall's heading: Muhriz son of al-Muka'bir, of Dabbah.
poems.text:
May all that I have amassed of substance be a sacrifice for my people, when War wraps together tribes with tribes !

What time Madhhij were told of us — and falsely were they told ! — that no defender would stand forth to protect our honour.

Our war-mill whirled but a little : then there fell on our foes a crushing blow wherefrom the great owls screech without ceasing.

Day-long the hyaenas of Mujairat visit them as they lie, and they give them to eat of their flesh — what a feasting !

They advanced towards us with their heads uplifted high in air, and we had prepared for them a Day that seemed as though it were days :

So that Hudhunnah — we left not a single hyaena there who had not for herself a carcase, the mangled remnants of a mighty chief.

All day long [War] crushed down the Sons of Ka'b with her breast, and the Day of the Sons of Nahd bethought itself of turning to darkness.
